overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights a dominant viewer preference for space and planetary 'What If' scenarios, as well as extreme cosmic anomalies. Videos framed around hypothetical planetary exploration (e.g., falling into liquid diamond planets, dark planets, and burning ice worlds) consistently drive higher views-per-day, strong like ratios, and active comments compared to standard psychological or biological facts. Recent items published in late September and October show significantly accelerated velocity.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (YlDuGu1vzAg) rapidly accumulated over 800 to 1,000+ views despite recent publishing dates, outperforming older biological facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes hypothetical planetary survival hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') combined with extreme visual environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing bizarre weather on exoplanets, such as 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0), generated strong engagement (20+ likes, rapid view velocity).
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form concepts featuring bizarre physics or extreme weather on real, verified exoplanets.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like song memory triggers ('The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' - Jc04LVKNd2s, 17 views) and generic brain memory facts generated very low engagement and minimal velocity.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychological micro-facts unless paired with a high-contrast physical threat or bizarre paradox.

weak_patterns.evidence: Standard animal facts (e.g., 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' - F1kXwuXuNgo) showed stagnant views compared to cosmic content.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal-related content into the cinematic animal survival or extreme deep-sea micro-story niches rather than basic trivia.
